'''Crispin William Gardiner''' (born 18 October 1942) is a New Zealand  physicist, who has worked in the fields of [[quantum optics]], [[ultracold atoms]] and [[stochastic process]]es, and is an Honorary Professor in the [[Department of Physics at the University of Otago|Department of Physics]] at the [[University of Otago]]. He has written about 120 journal articles and several books in the fields of [[quantum optics]], [[stochastic processes]] and [[ultracold atoms]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.co.nz/citations?user=c6v5W3sAAAAJ&hl=en|title = Crispin Gardiner's Google Scholar page}}</ref>

==Education==
Born in [[Hastings New Zealand]], Crispin Gardiner completed his undergraduate studies at the [[University of Auckland]] (B. Sc. 1964, M. Sc. 1965). He was awarded a research scholarship by the [[Royal Commission for the Exhibition of 1851]] in 1965, under which received his DPhil in 1968 from the [[Oxford University]] for research in elementary particle physics.

==Career==
Following his DPhil, Gardiner completed [[postdoctoral research]] in the group of
[[George Sudarshan]] at the [[Syracuse University]].

===University of Waikato, 1970–1995===
Gardiner was appointed to the faculty of the Physics Department of the [[University of Waikato]] in 1970, and was awarded a personal chair in physics in 1992, a position held until 1995.
When Gardiner arrived, the [[University of Waikato]] was only 5 years old, while the School of Science, which covered Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry, Biology and Earth Science, had only commenced teaching at the beginning of 1970, and no research facilities had been established.<ref name=ScienceWaikato>{{cite book|title= Celebrating 40 years of Science & Engineering|date=2009|publisher=University of Waikato}}</ref>

[[Dan Walls]] took up a position at Waikato in 1972,<ref name=frs/> and, working together,  he and Gardiner established a major research centre for theoretical quantum optics at Waikato, building active and productive collaborations with groups throughout the world.<ref name=frs>{{cite journal|last1=Knight|first1=Peter|author-link1=Peter Knight (scientist)|last2=Milburn|first2=Gerard J.|author-link2=Gerard J. Milburn|title=Daniel Frank Walls FRSNZ. 13 September 1942 — 12 May 1999|journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]|publisher=Royal Society publishing|year=2015|volume=61|issn=0080-4606|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2014.0019|doi-access=free|pages=531–540|s2cid=77660162}}</ref>

During this period

* He and [[Peter Drummond (physicist)|Peter Drummond]] developed the positive P-representation <ref name=Posp>{{Cite journal|journal=J Phys A|first1=P D|last1=Drummond|first2=C W|last2=Gardiner|title=Generalised P-Representations in Quantum Optics|date=1980|volume=13|pages=2353–2368|issue=7|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/13/7/018|bibcode=1980JPhA...13.2353D}}.</ref>
* He and [[Matthew Collett]] developed the input-output formalism <ref>{{cite journal|first1=C W|last1=Gardiner|first2=M J|last2=Collett|title=Input and Output in Damped Quantum Systems—Quantum stochastic Differential equations and the master equation|journal=Physical Review A|year=1985|volume=31|pages=3761–3774|issue=6|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.31.3761|pmid=9895956|bibcode=1985PhRvA..31.3761G}}</ref> for damped quantum systems, which they used <ref name=squeeze>{{cite journal|first1=M J|last1=Collett|first2=C W|last2=Gardiner|title=Squeezing of Intracavity and Travelling Wave Light Fields Produced in Parametric Amplification|journal=Physical Review A|date=1984|volume=30|pages=1386–1391|issue=3|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.30.1386|bibcode=1984PhRvA..30.1386C}}</ref> to predict and describe the spectrum of [[squeezed light]].
* He wrote the first (1985) edition of the book ''Stochastic Methods'',<ref>''Stochastic Methods''. Springer, (Berlin, Heidelberg and New York) 4th ed. 2004, {{ISBN|978-3-540-70712-7}} .</ref> now seen as a standard text in the field of applied stochastic processes.<ref>R P P P Grasman, E-J Wagenmakers, ''Rescue the Gardiner Book'', J Math Psychology 50 (2006) 431-435</ref>
* In 1986 he predicted the inhibition of atomic phase decays for a two-level atom coupled to a squeezed optical reservoir.<ref>{{cite journal|first=C W|last=Gardiner|title=Inhibition of Atomic Phase Decays by Squeezed Light: A Direct Effect of Squeezing|journal=Physical Review Letters|pages=1917–1920|volume=56|number=18|year=1986|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.1917|pmid=10032810|bibcode=1986PhRvL..56.1917G}}</ref> While challenging to realise in optical systems, the phenomenon was eventually observed in a superconducting qubit system affording sufficient reservoir control.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=K W|last1=Murch|first2 = S J|last2=Weber|
first3=K M|last3=Beck|first4=E|last4=Ginossar|first5=I|last5=Sidiqi|title=Reduction of the radiative decay of atomic coherence in squeezed vacuum|journal=Nature|pages=62–65|volume=499|year=2013|issue=7456|doi=10.1038/nature12264|pmid=23823794|arxiv=1301.6276|bibcode=2013Natur.499...62M|s2cid=205234358}}</ref>
* He wrote the first (1991) edition of the book ''Quantum Noise'',<ref>''Quantum Noise''. Springer, (Berlin, Heidelberg and New York) 3rd ed. 2004, {{ISBN|3-540-22301-0}} .</ref> (later editions were written in collaboration with [[Peter Zoller]]) which has become a standard text <ref>C W J Beenakker, ''Quantum Noise'', J Phys A 38 (2005), p7595</ref> in the fields of [[quantum optics]] and [[quantum stochastic methods]].
* In 1993 he developed (at the same time as a separate formulation by [[Howard Carmichael]]) the theory and application of [[cascaded quantum systems]], in which the optical output of one quantum system becomes the optical input for another quantum system.<ref name=cQSHJC>{{Cite journal|last=Carmichael|first=H J|date=1993|title=Quantum trajectory theory for cascaded open systems|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=70|issue=15|pages=2273–2276|bibcode=1993PhRvL..70.2273C|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.2273|pmid=10053519}}</ref><ref name=cQSCWG>{{Cite journal|last=Gardiner|first=C W|date=1993|title=Driving a quantum system with the output field from another driven quantum system|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=70|issue=15|pages=2269–2272|bibcode=1993PhRvL..70.2269G|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.2269|pmid=10053518}}</ref>

===Work in early childhood education, 1971–1991===
A very significant part of Gardiner's activity over the years 1971-1991 was as a parent activist, administrator and government consultant  in New Zealand early childhood education.  During this period very significant expansion of recognition, provision and government funding for early childhood education occurred.

In particular <ref name=CWCC>{{cite book|title=Concerning Women Considering Children: Battles of the NZ Childcare Association 1963-2003|author=[[Helen May]]|publisher=Te Tari Puna Ora o Aotearoa/New Zealand Childcare Association. Wellington, N.Z.}}</ref><ref name=LifeMb>{{cite book|title=Ngā kohinga kōrero a te aumangea: Kia mana te ara kōhungahunga ki Aotearoa: Life stories on the frontline: Growing a childcare movement in Aotearoa.|last1=May|first1=H|last2=Card|first2=A.|last3=Carroll-Lind|first3=J|publisher=Wellington, New Zealand: Te Rito Maioha Early Childhood New Zealand. |author1-link=Helen May }}</ref>

* He was one of the group which founded the "Campus Creche Society" in 1971, of which he was the secretary until 1974. The Campus Creche Society, advocated, and established the first Childcare Centre in the University of Waikato.
* He was elected to the executive of the N.Z. Childcare Association in 1975, becoming  Vice President 1983–1984.
* In 1976 he organised the Hamilton Day Care Centres Trust, which operated childcare services in Hamilton, and administered the government Childcare Subsidy in the full Waikato region.  He was chairman of The Trust 1976–1984.
* He worked for the Government in the development of policies and funding mechanisms for Early Childhood Education, as a member of several official boards and working parties, or as a consultant to the Ministry of Education.

===Independent researcher at Victoria University of Wellington, 1995–2005===
In 1995 he left the [[University of Waikato]] and for the next nine years worked as an independently funded researcher affiliated to [[Victoria University of Wellington]]. This was funded by the New Zealand R&D system, which was willing to fund individuals outside established institutions, and was motivated by the opportunity to leave the increasingly bureaucratic New Zealand University system.<ref name=Indres>{{cite journal|journal=New Scientist|date=16 July 2005|page=57|title=The Insider New Zealand–Time to go it alone?}}</ref>
During this period his work concentrated on the physics of [[Ultracold atoms]], developing a collaboration with [[Rob Ballagh]] of the [[University of Otago]]. They produced number of influential scientific publications, mainly concentrating on kinetic processes in Bose–Einstein condensates, funded by successive research contracts with the [[Marsden grant|Marsden Fund]]<ref name= trueBog>{{cite journal|first=C W|last=Gardiner|journal=Physical Review A|title=Particle-number-conserving Bogoliubov method which demonstrates the validity of the time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a highly condensed Bose gas|volume=56|date=1997|issue=2|pages=1414–1423|arxiv=quant-ph/9703005|bibcode=1997PhRvA..56.1414G|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.56.1414|s2cid=118927457}}</ref>
<ref name=Bosgro>{{cite journal|first1=C W|last1=Gardiner|first3=R J|last3=Ballagh|first4=M J|last4=Davis|first2=P|last2=Zoller| journal=Physical Review Letters|year=1997|volume=79|pages=1793–1796|title=Kinetics of Bose-Einstein condensation in a trap|issue=10|arxiv=quant-ph/9707037|bibcode=1997PhRvL..79.1793G|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.79.1793|s2cid=11879261}}
</ref>
<ref name=BH>{{cite journal|first1= D|last1=Jaksch|first2=C|last2=Bruder|first3=J I|last3=Cirac|first4=C W|last4=Gardiner|first5=P|last5=Zoller|title=Cold bosonic atoms in optical lattices|volume=81|pages=3108–3111|year=1998|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.3108|arxiv=cond-mat/9805329|bibcode=1998PhRvL..81.3108J|journal=Physical Review Letters|issue=15|s2cid=55578669}}</ref>
<ref name=vortexlatt>{{cite journal|journal=Physical Review Letters|first1=A A|last1=Penckwitt|first2=R J|last2 = Ballagh|first3=C W|last3=Gardiner|title=Nucleation, growth, and stabilization of Bose-Einstein condensate vortex lattices|volume=89|article-number=260402|date=2002|issue=26|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.89.260402|pmid=12484806|arxiv=cond-mat/0205037|bibcode=2002PhRvL..89z0402P}}</ref>
<ref name =SGPE>{{cite journal|first1= CW|last1=Gardiner|first2=J R|last2=Anglin|first3=T I A|last3=Fudge|title=The stochastic Gross–Pitaevskii equation|journal =J Phys B|volume=35|pages=1555–1582|year=2002|issue=6|doi=10.1088/0953-4075/35/6/310|arxiv=cond-mat/0112129|bibcode=2002JPhB...35.1555G}}</ref>
<ref name =SGPEII>{{cite journal|first1= CW|last1=Gardiner|first2=M J|last2=Davis|title=The stochastic Gross–Pitaevskii equation: II|journal =J Phys B|volume=36|pages=4731–4753|year=2003|issue=23|doi=10.1088/0953-4075/36/23/010|arxiv=cond-mat/0308044|bibcode=2003JPhB...36.4731G|s2cid=43776114}}</ref>
and in particular seven papers on [[quantum kinetic theory]]
.<ref name= QKI>{{cite journal |journal= Physical Review A|title=Quantum kinetic theory: A quantum kinetic master equation for condensation of a weakly interacting Bose gas without a trapping potential|first1=C W|last1=Gardiner|first2=P|last2=Zoller|date=1997|volume=55|issue=4|pages=2902–2921|arxiv=quant-ph/9611043|bibcode=1997PhRvA..55.2902G|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.55.2902|s2cid=119362659}}
</ref><ref name= QKII>{{cite journal |journal= Physical Review A|title=Quantum kinetic theory II|first1=D|last1=Jaksch|first2=C W|last2=Gardiner|first3=P|last3=Zoller|date=1997|volume=56|pages=575–586|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.56.575|arxiv=quant-ph/9701008|s2cid=119539688}}
</ref><ref name= QKIII>{{cite journal |journal= Physical Review A|title=Quantum kinetic theory III: Quantum kinetic master equation for strongly condensed trapped systems|first1=C W|last1=Gardiner|first2=P|last2=Zoller|date=1998|volume=58|issue=1|page=536|arxiv=cond-mat/9712002|bibcode=1998PhRvA..58..536G|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.58.536|s2cid=118983506}}
</ref><ref name= QKIV>{{cite journal |journal= Physical Review A|title=Quantum kinetic theory IV: Intensity and amplitude fluctuations of a Bose-Einstein condensate at finite temperature including trap loss|first1=D|last1=Jaksch|first2=C W|last2=Gardiner|first3=K M|last3=Gheri|first4=P|last4=Zoller|volume=58|page=1450|doi=10.1103/physreva.58.1450|arxiv=cond-mat/9712206|year=1998|issue=2|bibcode=1998PhRvA..58.1450J|s2cid=119075101}}
</ref><ref name= QKV>{{cite journal |journal= Physical Review A|title=Quantum kinetic theory V: Quantum kinetic master equation for mutual interaction of condensate and noncondensate|first1=C W|last1=Gardiner|first2=P|last2=Zoller|date=2000|volume=61|issue=3|article-number=033601|doi=10.1103/physreva.61.033601|arxiv=cond-mat/9905087|bibcode=2000PhRvA..61c3601G|s2cid=119472927}}
</ref><ref name= QKVI>{{cite journal |journal= Physical Review A|title=Quantum kinetic theory VI: The growth of a Bose-Einstein condensate|first1=M D|last1= Lee|first2=C W|last2=Gardiner|date=2000|volume=62|issue=3|article-number=033606|doi=10.1103/physreva.62.033606|arxiv=cond-mat/9912420|bibcode=2000PhRvA..62c3606L|s2cid=119399188}}
</ref><ref name= QKVII>{{cite journal |journal= Physical Review A|title=Quantum kinetic theory VII: The influence of vapor dynamics on condensate growth|first1=M J|last1=Davis|first2=C W|last2=Gardiner|first3=R J|last3=Ballagh|date=2000|volume=62|issue=6|article-number=063608|doi=10.1103/physreva.62.063608|arxiv=cond-mat/9912439|bibcode=2000PhRvA..62f3608D|s2cid=119012323|url=https://espace.library.uq.edu.au/view/UQ:249869/UQ249869_OA.pdf}}
</ref>

Gardiner characterised this period as "In terms of productivity, it has been the best 10 years research of my life."<ref name=Indres/>

===University of Otago, 2005–2013===
In 2005 he was appointed as a Research Professor in the [[Otago Department of Physics|Department of Physics]] at the [[University of Otago]]. In this period he was active in developing the [[University of Otago]] as a major research centre in [[ultracold atoms]], [[photonics]] and [[quantum optics]], which was named the ''Jack Dodd Centre'', after former Otago professor [[John Newton Dodd|Jack Dodd]]. During this period there was a major reorganisation of government research funding, commencing in 2006, which he and [[Rob Ballagh]] strongly criticised,<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Dominion Post|location=Wellington|first1=Crispin|last1=Gardiner|first2=Rob|last2=Ballagh|title=Science short-changed|date=31 May 2006}}</ref> on the grounds that this would exclude university research from any major funding.  Ultimately this aspect of the funding reform was not implemented, and in 2007 the ''Jack Dodd Centre'' was awarded a $6.4 million  research contract<ref>{{cite journal|journal=[[Otago Daily Times]] |date=19 July 2006|title=Otago Physicists Get a Cool $7m}}</ref> by the [[Foundation for Research, Science and Technology]].

From that time on, as director of the ''Jack Dodd Centre'', his role developed more into that of a research leader until his retirement in early 2013.

===Retirement===
On retirement he became an honorary professor at the [[University of Otago]] and in 2016 he accepted a position as visiting fellow at the [[Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information]] (IQOQI) in Innsbruck.

During this period he and [[Peter Zoller]] wrote the three books of ''The Quantum World of Ultra-Cold Atoms and Light''.<ref>See [http://europe.worldscientific.com/quantum-world-of-ultra-cold-atoms-and-light Quantum World Webpage] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142837/http://europe.worldscientific.com/quantum-world-of-ultra-cold-atoms-and-light |date=12 June 2018 }}.</ref>

== Books ==
* C W Gardiner:  ''A Handbook of Stochastic Methods''; Springer, Berlin Heidelberg, 1st ed.  1983; 2nd ed. 1985, 1989, 1998, 2001; 3rd Ed 2004, Russian Edition 1986 (Mir, Moscow)
* Crispin Gardiner:  ''Stochastic Methods''; Springer, Berlin Heidelberg, 2009 (A rewritten and updated 4th edition of ''A Handbook of Stochastic Methods'')
* Crispin Gardiner: ''Elements of Stochastic Methods''; AIP Publishing (online), Melville, New York, 2021, available at: https://doi.org/10.1063/9780735423718
* C W Gardiner:  ''Quantum Noise''; Springer, Berlin Heidelberg, 1st ed. 1991
* C W Gardiner and [[Peter Zoller]]:  ''Quantum Noise'';  Springer, Berlin Heidelberg, 2nd ed. 1999, 3rd ed. 2004
* Crispin Gardiner and [[Peter Zoller]]: ''The Quantum World of Ultra-Cold Atoms and Light Book I:  Foundations of Quantum Optics'', Imperial College Press, London and Singapore 2014.
* Crispin Gardiner and [[Peter Zoller]]: ''The Quantum World of Ultra-Cold Atoms and Light Book II:  Physics of Quantum Optical Devices'', Imperial College Press, London and Singapore 2015.
* Crispin Gardiner and [[Peter Zoller]]: ''The Quantum World of Ultra-Cold Atoms and Light Book III:  Ultra-Cold Atoms'', World Scientific, London and Singapore 2014.

== Awards and honours ==
* 1983   Fellow of the New Zealand Institute of Physics
* 1984   Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]
* 1990   Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand (Until 2011)
* 2000   Honorary Dr. Rer. Nat.  from the University of Innsbruck: ''In recognition of his outstanding scientific merit in the field of theoretical quantum optics''
